title: Once in Royal David's City
description: Cecil Frances Alexander's Christmas hymn to Henry John Gauntlett's tune Irby, in the four parts Gauntlett harmonized for Hymns Ancient and Modern (1868), for 2 to 4 singers: verses 1, 2 and 6, slow and steady. The tune climbs to its high E on "Mary was that mother mild" and comes home on "Jesus Christ her little Child."

credits.arrangement: Henry John Gauntlett's four parts (Hymns Ancient and Modern, 1868), adapted by Stackapella

licence.words: public domain: Cecil Frances Alexander died 1895 (Julian's Dictionary of Hymnology, 1907 edition: "d. at Londonderry, Oct. 12, 1895"); first printed in her Hymns for Little Children (1848), p. 30, in six stanzas (Julian); sung here as Hymns Ancient and Modern (1868), No. 361, prints them, verses 1, 2 and 6 of the six; verses 1 and 2 read the same in the First American Edition of Hymns for Little Children (Philadelphia: Hooker, [1850]), p. 30, No. 11 (archive.org/details/hymnsforlittlech00alex/page/n35), apart from capitals and punctuation (verse 3, not sung here, has "lovely maiden" there and "lowly maiden" in the 1868 book)
licence.tune: public domain: Henry John Gauntlett died 21 February 1876 (Grove's Dictionary of Music and Musicians); the 1868 book's Index of Tunes (p. xxviii) gives "Irby" with composer "Dr. Gauntlett", and its preface (p. ix) says the tune was "inserted by leave of Mr. Masters", so it was printed before, in Gauntlett's Christmas Carols (Masters, about 1849, a lead: not seen)
licence.arrangement: Gauntlett's own four parts, "harmonized for them" (the 1868 preface, p. ix) and signed "Harmonized or Arranged by Dr. Gauntlett" in the Index of Tunes (Gauntlett died 1876; the book's musical editor William Henry Monk died 1889; public domain): his tune, key and most of his chords, with the lower parts revoiced for 2 to 4 beginners. One note a syllable in every lower part: his passing quavers under "Da-vid's" and "cat-tle" (tenor), and the quaver runs that open lines 5 and 6 (bass C, D, E, F sharp and G, A, B; tenor B, C, D; alto G, F sharp, G), become one held note. The alto takes the chord's third for the duet: B3 under "Once" and "roy-" (his D4); E4 on "vid's", over D in the bass (his D4 then F sharp 4); B3, D4, F sharp 4 on "Stood a low-" (his D4, G4, G4), the chord on "a" B minor (his E minor) and on "low-" D over A (his G over B), then G over B on "ly"; E4 under "laid her" over A7 (his C sharp 4, which the tenor takes); C4, C4, B3, D4 on "Ma-ry was that" (his G4, G4 and quavers G, F sharp, G), over C, C, G and G over B (his C, C over E, G); E4 and F sharp 4 on "mo-ther" over A minor and D7 (his D7 with a suspended fourth, then D7). The bass sings D3 on "in" (his A2), holds B2 through "roy-al" (his B2, G2), sings D3, B2, A2, B2 on "Stood a low-ly" (his G3, E3, B2, G2) and A2 on "mo-" (his D3); the tenor answers with B3 at the starts of lines 1 and 3, F sharp 3 on "a" and D4 on "ly", lies low on line 5 (G3, E3, D3) so no two parts move in fifths or octaves, and rises to G3 on its last word (his D4). In the last line the alto sings G4, G4, F sharp 4, G4 on "Je-sus Christ her" (his E4, G4, D4, D4), the bass A2 on "sus" and "Christ" and B2 on "her" (his E3, G3, G3), and the tenor his C4 on "sus" and "Christ", so the chords are C, A minor seven, D7 over A and G over B (his C, C over E, G and G). Breaths written in for beginners: each line's last note gives up half a beat, except the song's last; where a line of verse 2 has a syllable more than the tune's line ("low-ly", "Ho-ly"), its last minim is sung as two crotchets in every part. The Amen is left out
licence.source: Hymns Ancient and Modern for use in the Services of the Church, with Accompanying Tunes, compiled and arranged under the musical editorship of William Henry Monk, with Appendix (London: printed for the proprietors by W. Clowes and Sons, 1868; the Appendix's preface dated September 1868), No. 361, "For the Young", headed "The child Jesus", in four parts in G major (one sharp), barred in four crotchets with a two-crotchet pickup to each line, in its printed key here (G); the music read from the University of Toronto Faculty of Music copy at archive.org/details/hymnsancientmode00unse_0/page/n551, the words on n552, the preface p. ix at n14 and the Index of Tunes p. xxviii at n33; checked against a later printing of the Revised and Enlarged Edition (London: printed for the proprietors by William Clowes and Sons, Limited; undated, catalogued 1874 under New York, Pott, Young and Co.), No. 329, p. 251, archive.org/details/hymnsancientmode00monk/page/n264, the same tune and harmony note for note in every place compared (lines 5 and 6 in full), with "Mother" capitalised and dynamics added
